projects.title: Aether OS Interactive Spatial Window
projects.desc: An award-winning viewport framework operating custom spatial coordinates using raw JS layouts.
projects.content: Aether OS is an experimental spatial viewport manager designed for modern desktop web applications. It uses hardware-accelerated transform layers to let users snap, scale, and stack multiple windows seamlessly on a virtual desktop canvas.

projects.title: Nova Minimalist Component Core
projects.desc: A hyper-optimized component foundry yielding zero layout jank on standard browser renders.
projects.content: Nova Core is a high-performance design system library built using utility-first styling tokens. It compiles to zero runtime CSS overhead, achieving sub-millisecond layout passes and eliminating layout shifts on dynamic screens.

projects.title: Decentralized Crypto Vault
projects.desc: A secure crypto dashboard designed to track assets, complete with rich SVG data charting.
projects.content: CryptVault is a student capstone project creating a secure, client-side dashboard for decentralized finance networks. Features offline keys storage, custom SVG path charting for historical prices, and MetaMask integration.

projects.title: AI Scholar Literature Finder
projects.desc: An automated agent search tool integrating NCBI PubMed APIs and semantic summaries.
projects.content: AIScholar is an AI assistant that queries literature databases like PubMed and arXiv, extracts key methodology abstracts, and utilizes local language model embeddings to construct comparative research grids.

blogs.title: The Typography of Silence: Why whitespace dictates SaaS visual identity
blogs.desc: An investigation into how high-fashion typography parameters dictate standard interface conversion rates and mental cognitive load.
blogs.content: Whitespace is not empty space; it is a structural element. In high-converting SaaS interfaces, whitespace guides the user’s eye, establishes visual hierarchy, and reduces cognitive overload. By studying high-fashion typography variables, we can apply editorial padding parameters to layout structures to elevate brand identity and drive conversion.

blogs.title: Designing for the GPU: Shifting the rendering load away from JS cycles
blogs.desc: A technical look at transform layers, viewport matrices, and compositing variables that result in smooth scroll architectures.
blogs.content: Smooth scrolling is achieved when the browser runs at 60fps (or 120fps). Standard JavaScript animations block the main thread. By shifting layout transformations to CSS compositor variables (using transform3d, will-change, and translateZ), we utilize the GPU directly, ensuring a lag-free layout scroll experience even with heavy coordinate grids.

blogs.title: The Tactile Web: Fusing physical textures with digital layout layers
blogs.desc: Exploring how micro-interactions, spring physics, and subtle gradients create depth in modern interfaces.
blogs.content: We experience the physical world through touch and material weight. The digital interface can simulate this weight using spring animations and coordinate depths. Designing with layers that slightly overlap and translate based on scroll speed mimics physical parallax, making the interface feel alive and tactile.

blogs.title: CSS Subgrid & Container Queries: Reimagining grid dependencies
blogs.desc: A detailed look at modular card rendering systems that scale dynamically to layout grids.
blogs.content: CSS container queries allow components to own their responsive styling based on their parent container width rather than the screen viewport. Together with CSS Subgrid, cards inside nested grids align perfectly to the master layout grid, preventing layout shifts and creating highly modular component foundries.

timeline.footerText: Focusing on statistical modeling, machine learning pipelines, and building clean web systems.

highlights.label: 01. Good design is unobtrusive
highlights.detail: Products fulfilling a purpose are like tools. They are neither decorative objects nor works of art.

highlights.label: 02. As little design as possible
highlights.detail: Less, but better – because it concentrates on the essential aspects of the product.

highlights.label: 01. Establish visual hierarchy
highlights.detail: Contrast is key. Don't just make elements bigger; use weight, scale, and color to guide the eye.

highlights.label: 02. Design with real content
highlights.detail: Placeholders can mask layout flaws. Real data forces you to solve actual constraints early.

highlights.label: 01. Eliminate needless choices
highlights.detail: If something requires a user to pause and think about how to use it, the design has failed.

highlights.label: 02. Optimize for scanning
highlights.detail: We don't read web pages line-by-line; we scan them looking for landmarks that match our goals.
